slides.title: Invisible Forces in Your Pocket
slides.subtitle: How microscopic silicon structures detect physical orientation instantly.
slides.body: Mobile apps know when you tilt your device, but how does raw physics translate into application state?
slides.deep_dive: Bridging physical mass movement with digital event loops requires hardware-software co-design.
slides.key_fact: Silicon fingers measure microscopic shifts invisible to the naked eye.

slides.title: The Microscopic Spring Scale
slides.body: Imagine a tiny weight suspended by microscopic silicon springs inside your phone chip.

steps.title: Inertia Shift
steps.desc: When you move the phone, the tiny suspended weight lags behind.

steps.title: Distance Change
steps.desc: The gap between movable fingers and fixed electrodes narrows on one side.

steps.title: Electrical Output
steps.desc: This physical displacement alters electrical capacitance instantly.

slides.key_fact: Capacitance changes directly reflect physical acceleration magnitude.
slides.why_it_matters: Translates physical motion into measurable electrical properties.

slides.title: From Voltage to Vector
slides.body: The hardware-to-software pipeline converts raw capacitance into usable Cartesian coordinates.
slides.input: Raw analog voltage pulses from microscopic capacitive plates.
slides.processing: Amplification, analog-to-digital conversion, and low-pass hardware filtering.
slides.output: Clean three-axis acceleration values along X, Y, and Z vectors.
slides.key_fact: Analog signals become discrete digital vectors per second.
slides.why_it_matters: Provides standard numeric inputs for application logic.

slides.title: Balancing Precision and Power
slides.body: High-frequency sensor sampling delivers precise tracking at the cost of battery life.
slides.key_fact: Sampling rate directly dictates energy consumption rates.
slides.why_it_matters: Engineers must match sensor frequency to specific feature needs.

slides.title: Raw Data vs Filtered Reality
slides.body: Never trust raw accelerometer data directly for user motion without separating gravity.
before_items: Using raw accelerometer for step counters
Treating gravity pull as user movement
slides.key_fact: Gravity and linear motion must be mathematically separated.
slides.why_it_matters: Prevents erratic UI behavior and false gesture triggers.

slides.title: Sensor Fusion at Scale
slides.body: Modern operating systems combine multiple hardware sensors to build a reliable world model.

_story.title: Your Phone Senses Gravity's Invisible Pull
_story.hook: Did You Know your phone can actually 'feel' gravity? 🤯
_story.headline: The Tiny Tech That Tells Your Phone If It's Falling
_story.fact_summary: Inside your smartphone are tiny accelerometers, microscopic springs and weights that constantly measure motion and the force of gravity. When you drop your phone, these sensors detect a sudden change – a feeling of 'freefall' – allowing the phone to instantly know it's plummeting. This incredible tech not only powers features like auto-rotate but can even detect if you've taken a tumble!
_story.source: Modern smartphone engineering, MEMS accelerometer principles
